title: Single-point weather proxy validation against OCCTO actuals
purpose: Quantify the single-point limitation rather than merely concede it. Capacity-weighted spatial aggregation is out of scope for this revision; this phase measures what the one-city proxy does and does not capture, and audits the capacity table it is scaled by.

proxy_skill.note: The proxy is a resource index in arbitrary units, so it is rescaled to the target by least squares through the origin before error metrics are reported. Correlations are scale-free. PV and wind targets are POTENTIAL output (realised + curtailed), because the proxy models the resource rather than the dispatch decision.

capacity_integrity.verdict: The nameplate table is understated: realised potential output exceeds it in 7 of 16 area-channels. A constant per-area scale factor is absorbed by the learner, so the proxies used as REGRESSORS are unaffected. The cross-area PV/peak saturation index is NOT: it inherits the error directly, so a vintage-free index is computed below and both are reported.

saturation_indices.reading: The realised index is observable and carries no capacity vintage. Where the two indices rank areas differently, any cross-area statistic computed on the table index is sensitive to the stale capacity figures, and the paper must show its conclusion under both. Feeding this index into the phase55 slope/rho tests is the follow-up.
